title: hotfix: enforce-slo-circuit-breaker-load-shedding-with-regional-failover
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: tighter SLO enforcement for gateway and runtime circuit breakers; added emergency load-shedding mode and automated regional failover when capacity falls below configured thresholds. Backwards-compatible configuration flags added.
description:
Context: A partial outage on 2026-02-27 (INC-2026-02-27) showed that under sustained overload in us-west, our runtime allowed requests to queue long enough to violate customer SLOs and cascade into connection churn. Root cause: SLO enforcement path in the gateway and runtime circuit-breaker thresholds were too permissive, and regional failover was not triggered until after severe latency degradation. This PR is an emergency hotfix to enforce SLOs earlier, enable deterministic load-shedding, and trigger regional failover proactively.

Changes in this PR: consolidated SLO calculation to a single enforcement path, introduced an "emergency" load-shedding mode with progressive shedding based on queue depth and observed P95 latency, tightened circuit-breaker tripping thresholds for headroom protection, and added a regional failover hook that will route to the next region when available capacity falls below the configured SLO headroom.

Checklist: - [x] Add stricter circuit-breaker thresholds and unit tests for edge cases - [x] Implement emergency load-shedding mode and integration tests - [x] Add regional failover routing + unit tests - [x] Add canary rollout config and observability/metrics - [x] Run canary in us-west for 30m and monitor SLOs

Compatibility and rollout: The changes are backward compatible: new behavior enabled via feature flag defaulted ON for production hotfix. Operators can opt-out per-cluster via config map. Rollout: canary -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 2 hours with automated rollback on SLO regressions.

Motivation: Prevent cascading failures and ensure customers continue to meet latency SLOs even under partial regional capacity loss. This reduces customer-visible errors and avoids manual emergency failovers.

Testing: unit tests, integration tests (simulated queue pressure), and a short canary in us-west. CI initially failed on linting; fixed formatting and re-ran CI. All checks green at merge.

Operational notes: added new metrics (slo.enforcer.tripped, slo.enforcer.shed_rate, region.failover.triggered) and dashboards; alert tweaks in SLO paging rules to avoid alert storms during controlled shedding.

Rollback: run scripts/rollback_hotfix.sh to restore previous circuit-breaker thresholds and disable emergency mode; documented in runbook.

Related: Linear ENG-7123, SRE-124; incident: INC-2026-02-27.
